finding: Rates of cesarean delivery on maternal request among all live births increased throughout the study period, from 1% in 1999 to 1.62% in 2015.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery on maternal request was associated with an increased risk of venous thromboembolism, myocardial infarction, sepsis, disseminated intravascular coagulation, death, and prolonged hospital stay and a lower risk of postpartum hemorrhage.
